meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Даже если вы там все беременны!
examples.trans: Even if all of you there are pregnant!

examples.text: Катя даже собирается к нему домой переехать.
examples.trans: Katya is even planning to move into his home.

examples.text: Лёва! Откуда Лёва? Его даже на кухне не было.
examples.trans: Lyova! Where did Lyova come from? He wasn't even in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Не нравится наша кухня — никто вас здесь не держит.
examples.trans: If you don't like our cuisine, nobody is keeping you here.

examples.text: Это что за взрыв ты устроила на моей кухне?
examples.trans: What kind of explosion did you stage in my kitchen?

examples.text: На моей кухне тебе всегда будет пятнадцать.
examples.trans: In my kitchen you will always be fifteen.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'threw, tossed in', paired with 'бросать'.

examples.text: Это я бросила. Лёве тоже жена нужна.
examples.trans: I tossed it in. Lyova needs a wife too.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила.
examples.trans: My wife has left me.

examples.text: Брось мяч!
examples.trans: Throw the ball!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если женщина, жди неприятностей и не жди чаевых.
examples.trans: If it is a woman, expect trouble and don't expect tips.

examples.text: Зачем жену уважаемого человека обидела, а?
examples.trans: Why did you offend the wife of an important man, huh?

examples.text: Это не Виктория Сергеевна. Это я этой женщине хамил.
examples.trans: It wasn't Viktoria Sergeyevna. I was the one who was rude to that woman.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.text: Машина нужна на пару часов.
examples.trans: I need a car for a couple of hours.

examples.text: Твоей дочери нужно помочь переехать на новую квартиру.
examples.trans: Your daughter needs help moving to a new apartment.

examples.text: Это я бросила. Лёве тоже жена нужна.
examples.trans: I tossed it in. Lyova needs a wife too.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно. В конце концов, ребёнок не виноват.
examples.trans: Fine. After all, the child is not at fault.

examples.text: Ладно, хорошо. Сейчас приеду.
examples.trans: Fine, all right. I will come over now.

examples.text: Ладно, не хочешь хорошего, включу плохого.
examples.trans: Fine, if you don't want the good father, I will turn on the bad one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, Лёва так Лёва. Где счастливчик?
examples.trans: Fine, Lyova it is. Where is the lucky guy?

examples.text: Где наш счастливчик?
examples.trans: Where is our lucky guy?

examples.text: А где дамочка?
examples.trans: And where is the little lady?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частливчик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'lucky guy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, Лёва так Лёва. Где счастливчик?
examples.trans: Fine, Lyova it is. Where is the lucky guy?

examples.text: Где наш счастливчик?
examples.trans: Where is our lucky guy?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не нравится наша кухня — никто вас здесь не держит.
examples.trans: If you don't like our cuisine, nobody is keeping you here.

examples.text: Наша проблема сейчас в клубе в трёх кварталах отсюда.
examples.trans: Our problem is currently at a club three blocks from here.

examples.text: Где наш счастливчик?
examples.trans: Where is our lucky guy?
